content: Same thing has been happening in tech for decades. Technology gets captured by a bigco, they kill all the inspiration, in order to lock it down it for ROI. There are developers inside these companies who believe in open systems, as lawyers believe in the rule of law, and if we support them from outside, we can probably change the behavior, make them aware of the cost when they destroy something of value they don't own, as they are doing with the web as it was defined by Netscape and Microsoft before. None of these companies were restrained, not by public opinion or court decisions. Now we may have the political power to be heard, and we know how to protect the web where we don't have a good idea of how to do it for AI yet. We can start with the web, and make sure they don't act like owners of the tech, redefining the web via a browser monopoly. In the antitrust case against Microsoft in the 1990's they were looking at the wrong pairing, they saw the problem between Windows and Office, when the real thing that needed to be separated from MS, as with Google, is the web browser.
